bug_semantics: NLTK Downloader._download_package downloads a corpus/model archive over HTTP via urlopen, writes the bytes to disk, then extracts with unzip/_unzip_iter without comparing the received file to the package-index checksum. MD5 (later SHA-256) hashing exists only in _pkg_status() as a pre-download installed/stale check, so a MITM, DNS-poisoned, or malicious-mirror response is extracted and treated as trusted NLTK data (CWE-494).
flaw_origin: The missing post-download integrity check was first written in 2008 when Edward Loper added nltk/downloader.py: _download_package already downloaded then unzipped, and _pkg_status already hashed the on-disk package only to decide INSTALLED vs STALE. Later SHA-256 index work and the 3.9.3 zip-slip hardening never wired that hash into the post-download path.

GHSA-gf32-cmjh-8m9v is the NVD import of the same CVE.

reasoning: The CVE/GHSA describe a real CWE-494 gap: NLTK's downloader extracts a just-downloaded package without verifying it against the index checksum. CVE.org is PUBLISHED and GHSA-5wp5-5229-5g6q is not withdrawn, so this is not FALSE_POSITIVE; the claimed patched boundary 3.9.3 is simply wrong. On 3.9.2 and 3.9.3, _download_package still writes the HTTP body then unzips, while _pkg_status uses the checksum only as a pre-download stale check. git log -L on that download-then-unzip region reconstructs to the 2008 first add of nltk/downloader.py (fa242f5e10511cb2400396ebb56964becef12799); the immediate parent tree lacks the file, and later black/pyupgrade/unzip-iterator edits are carriers, not first-writes. The same commit already shipped md5_hexdigest and used it only in _pkg_status, so the missing post-download check is original design, not a later regression. Closure is 7a5740af89feeb739193db766e11e85dfe78339c (PR #3625), which is the first public-history commit that hashes the temp file before os.replace/extract; it is not in 3.9.3/3.9.4 and first ships in v3.10.0. AI attribution is judged only on the BIC commit object: human author/committer Edward Loper in 2008 with no AI/bot trailers, so NOT_AI.
